options.content:
Since 2023 anchors dragged along the floor of the Baltic have cut cables and a gas pipeline
(Balticconnector, C-Lion1, Estlink 2 among them). This dashboard watches for the signature,
live, and raises a **Grafana alert** for every cargo ship or tanker that lingers over one.

- **Ships**: [Digitraffic](https://www.digitraffic.fi/en/marine-traffic/), Fintraffic's AIS
  network: the latest position, name and type of every ship its Finnish coastal stations hear,
  through the gateway (cached 30 s). The Gulf of Finland, the Bothnian Sea and the northern
  Baltic, roughly 57.5°–66° N; the southern Baltic is out of its range. A ship counts while it
  was heard in the last 15 minutes. Flag: the first three digits of the MMSI.
- **Cables and pipelines** (`datasets/baltic-cables`, built on each instance): telecom cables
  from [TeleGeography's Submarine Cable Map](https://www.submarinecablemap.com) (CC BY-SA 4.0),
  power cables from [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org) (ODbL), gas pipelines from
  [EMODnet Human Activities](https://emodnet.ec.europa.eu/en/human-activities) (CC BY 4.0).
- **Fences**: a kilometre each side of each cable, less 5 km around every port (EMODnet) and
  cable landing, where ships are expected to wait.

**The alert** (`provisioning/alerting/baltic-cable-watch.yaml`): a query on the server DuckDB
finds the cargo ships and tankers inside a fence that are slow (under 3 knots) or at anchor;
a SQL expression makes each row an alert, labelled by ship and cable. **Pending** (amber) as a
ship arrives, **firing** (red) after 15 minutes; at anchor and moving 2–6 knots, the sign of a
dragged anchor, it is critical. The map is Kepler Plus's **Active alerts**: each alert drawn on
its ship (Entity label `mmsi`) and each fence coloured by the alerts naming its cable (Zone
label `cable`), blue when quiet.

**Filters**: the server reads the ships, the cables and the alerts on each refresh (every
minute) and hands them to **Chaski**, DuckDB in your browser; the filters on the left are
answered there, at once, by the map (ships, alerts, cables and fences), the cards and the tables.

A slow ship over a cable is not an accusation: anchorages off busy ports lie over pipelines,
and ships wait there for a berth. The watch shows where to look.

spec.description: Filter the cables and pipelines by kind or by name: the map draws only those and their fences, and the tables and cards count only the ships over them.
spec.title: Cables and pipelines

spec.rawSql:
SELECT c.cable AS "Cable", c.kind AS "Kind", c.km AS "Km",
       count(DISTINCT l.mmsi)::DOUBLE AS "Lingering", c.url,
       c.centre_lat + (epoch_ms(now()) % 10) * 1e-6 AS clat, c.centre_lng AS clng
FROM (SELECT * FROM $cables WHERE $__crossfilter($cableFilters)) c
LEFT JOIN (SELECT mmsi, cable FROM $lingering WHERE mmsi IN (SELECT mmsi FROM $ships WHERE $__crossfilter($shipFilters))) l ON l.cable = c.cable
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY "Lingering" DESC, c.kind, c.cable

spec.description: The cables and pipelines in the waters Digitraffic hears, their length in the Baltic (km) and the ships of the ship filters lingering over each now. A click on the name flies the map to the cable, or opens its source.
spec.title: Cables and pipelines in the watched waters

spec.rawSql:
-- Server side: the rule state history Grafana keeps (anyone can read it),
-- over the panel range: one row per change of state of one alert.
SET VARIABLE history = 'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/rules/history?ruleUID=baltic-cable-watch&limit=20000'
  || '&from=' || epoch(CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP))::BIGINT || '&to=' || epoch(CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP))::BIGINT;
WITH frame AS (
  SELECT content::JSON AS j FROM read_text(getvariable('history'))
), changes AS (
  SELECT make_timestamp(unnest(from_json(j -> '$.data.values[0]', '["BIGINT"]'))) AS time,
         unnest(from_json(j -> '$.data.values[1]', '["VARCHAR"]')) AS text,
         unnest(from_json(j -> '$.data.values[3]', '["VARCHAR"]')) AS state
  FROM frame
), spans AS (
  -- An alert is its labels; each state holds until its next change.
  SELECT split_part(text, ' - ', 1) AS alert, state, time AS since,
         coalesce(lead(time) OVER (PARTITION BY split_part(text, ' - ', 1) ORDER BY time), now()::TIMESTAMP) AS until
  FROM changes
), minutes AS (
  SELECT unnest(generate_series(time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP)),
                                least(CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP), now()::TIMESTAMP), INTERVAL 1 MINUTE)) AS time
)
SELECT m.time,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.state LIKE 'Alerting%')::DOUBLE AS firing,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.state LIKE 'Pending%')::DOUBLE AS pending
FROM minutes m
LEFT JOIN spans s ON s.since <= m.time AND m.time < s.until
GROUP BY m.time
ORDER BY m.time

spec.description: The alerts of the rule minute by minute over the last 24 hours, rebuilt from the state history Grafana keeps for it: firing (red, lingering 15 minutes or more) and pending (amber), stacked. Not filtered.
spec.title: Alerts over the last 24 hours

spec.rawSql:
-- The ships the filters keep, for the Fleet layer: lingering over a cable in
-- red, cargo ships and tankers in white, the rest in grey.
SELECT mmsi, ship, label, type, flag, status, knots, course, destination, watch, alert, over_cable, time, latitude, longitude
FROM $ships
WHERE $__crossfilter($shipFilters)

-- The fences of the cables the filters keep, as the zones of the alerts: Active
-- alerts colours each by the alerts whose cable label names it.
SELECT cable, kind, fence AS geometry
FROM $cables
WHERE $__crossfilter($cableFilters)

-- The cables the filters keep. Called name, not cable: a frame with the zone
-- column and a geometry would be read as zones too.
SELECT cable AS name, kind, operator, km, geometry
FROM $cables
WHERE $__crossfilter($cableFilters)

Ships Digitraffic heard in the last 15 minutes (cargo and tankers white, lingering over a cable red), the cables and pipelines (telecom teal, power yellow, gas purple) and their fences, coloured by the alert rule: red firing, amber pending, blue quiet.

spec.rawSql:
-- lat and lng: where the map goes when it starts to follow the ship.
SELECT ship AS "Ship", mmsi, cable AS "Cable", alert AS "Alert", since AS "Since", latitude AS lat, longitude AS lng
FROM $lingering
WHERE mmsi IN (SELECT mmsi FROM $ships WHERE $__crossfilter($shipFilters))
  AND cable IN (SELECT cable FROM $cables WHERE $__crossfilter($cableFilters))
ORDER BY CASE alert WHEN 'Alert' THEN 0 WHEN 'Watching' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, since, ship

spec.description: Every ship heard in the last 15 minutes, in the browser, loaded on each refresh.
spec.name: ships

query.rawSql:
SET force_download = true;
-- The setting would outlive this query on the pooled connection it ran on, and stop the range reads of every Parquet read there later, so the result goes through a temp table (one per connection) and the setting is put back before it is returned.
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE fd_baltic_1 AS
WITH heard AS (
  -- Digitraffic: the latest position of each ship its AIS stations heard; a ship
  -- counts while it was heard in the last 15 minutes.
  SELECT unnest(features, recursive := true)
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/digitraffic/ais/locations', columns = {features:
    'STRUCT(geometry STRUCT(coordinates DOUBLE[]), properties STRUCT(mmsi BIGINT, sog DOUBLE, cog DOUBLE, navStat INTEGER, timestampExternal BIGINT))[]'})
), vessels AS (
  -- Name, type and destination, from the static AIS messages of each ship.
  SELECT * FROM read_json('http://feeds/digitraffic/ais/vessels',
    columns = {mmsi: 'BIGINT', name: 'VARCHAR', shipType: 'INTEGER', destination: 'VARCHAR'})
), ships AS (
  SELECT h.mmsi::VARCHAR AS mmsi,
    coalesce(nullif(trim(v.name), ''), 'MMSI ' || h.mmsi) AS ship,
    -- AIS ship types, named so the Fleet layer picks a fitting silhouette.
    CASE
      WHEN v.shipType BETWEEN 70 AND 79 THEN 'Cargo'
      WHEN v.shipType BETWEEN 80 AND 89 THEN 'Tanker'
      WHEN v.shipType BETWEEN 60 AND 69 THEN 'Passenger'
      WHEN v.shipType BETWEEN 40 AND 49 THEN 'High-speed craft'
      WHEN v.shipType = 30 THEN 'Fishing'
      WHEN v.shipType IN (31, 32, 52) THEN 'Tug'
      WHEN v.shipType = 35 THEN 'Military vessel'
      WHEN v.shipType = 36 THEN 'Sailing'
      WHEN v.shipType = 37 THEN 'Pleasure boat'
      WHEN v.shipType = 50 THEN 'Pilot boat'
      WHEN v.shipType = 51 THEN 'Rescue boat'
      WHEN v.shipType = 55 THEN 'Patrol boat'
      ELSE 'Other vessel'
    END AS type,
    coalesce(f.flag, 'MID ' || (h.mmsi // 1000000)) AS flag,
    nullif(trim(v.destination), '') AS destination,
    h.coordinates[2] AS latitude, h.coordinates[1] AS longitude,
    -- 102.3 knots and 360° are how AIS says not available.
    CASE WHEN h.sog < 102.3 THEN h.sog END AS knots,
    CASE WHEN h.cog < 360 THEN h.cog END AS course,
    CASE h.navStat WHEN 0 THEN 'Under way' WHEN 1 THEN 'At anchor' WHEN 2 THEN 'Not under command'
      WHEN 3 THEN 'Restricted manoeuvrability' WHEN 4 THEN 'Constrained by draught' WHEN 5 THEN 'Moored'
      WHEN 6 THEN 'Aground' WHEN 7 THEN 'Fishing' WHEN 8 THEN 'Sailing' ELSE 'Not reported' END AS status,
    h.navStat AS nav_status,
    -- Watched: cargo ships and tankers, the ships whose anchors have cut cables.
    coalesce(v.shipType BETWEEN 70 AND 89, false) AS watched,
    make_timestamp(h.timestampExternal * 1000) AS heard
  FROM heard h
  LEFT JOIN vessels v USING (mmsi)
  LEFT JOIN 'http://feeds/datasets/baltic-cables/flags.parquet' f ON f.mid = h.mmsi // 1000000
  WHERE make_timestamp(h.timestampExternal * 1000) > now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE
    AND h.coordinates[2] BETWEEN -90 AND 90
), fences AS (
  -- The cables in the waters the Digitraffic stations hear, with their fences.
  SELECT cable, kind, operator, url, km, line, fence
  FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/baltic-cables/cables.parquet'
  WHERE ST_Intersects(line, ST_MakeEnvelope(17, 57.5, 33, 66.5))
), lingering AS (
  -- A watched ship inside a fence, slow (under 3 knots) or at anchor and
  -- moving under 6 (an anchor dragged along the seabed): one row per ship and
  -- cable.
  SELECT s.*, c.cable, c.kind,
    CASE WHEN s.nav_status = 1 AND s.knots >= 2 THEN 'Dragging anchor'
         WHEN s.nav_status = 1 THEN 'At anchor'
         ELSE 'Slow' END AS signature
  FROM ships s JOIN fences c ON ST_Contains(c.fence, ST_Point(s.longitude, s.latitude))
  WHERE s.watched AND (s.knots < 3 OR (s.nav_status = 1 AND s.knots < 6))
), api AS (
  -- Grafana's own alerting API, as an anonymous viewer reads it: this rule's
  -- alerts, one per ship and cable.
  SELECT unnest(from_json(r -> '$.alerts', '["JSON"]')) AS a
  FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json(g -> '$.rules', '["JSON"]')) AS r
        FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json(content::JSON -> '$.data.groups', '["JSON"]')) AS g
              FROM read_text('http://localhost:3000/api/prometheus/grafana/api/v1/rules')))
  WHERE r ->> '$.uid' = 'baltic-cable-watch'
), alerts AS (
  SELECT a ->> '$.labels.mmsi' AS mmsi, a ->> '$.labels.cable' AS cable,
         CASE a ->> '$.state' WHEN 'Alerting' THEN 'Alert' WHEN 'Pending' THEN 'Watching' ELSE 'Clear' END AS alert,
         (a ->> '$.activeAt')::TIMESTAMPTZ AS since
  FROM api
)
-- Server side, on each load and refresh: every ship heard in the last 15
-- minutes, with what it is doing over the cables and the gravest state of its
-- alerts (Alert firing, Watching pending).
SELECT s.mmsi, s.ship, s.ship || ' · ' || s.flag AS label, s.type, s.flag, s.status,
       round(s.knots, 1) AS knots, s.course, s.destination,
       CASE WHEN l.cables IS NOT NULL THEN 'Lingering'
            WHEN s.watched THEN 'Cargo or tanker' ELSE 'Other' END AS watch,
       coalesce(a.alert, 'No alert') AS alert,
       l.cables AS over_cable, s.heard AS time, s.latitude, s.longitude
FROM ships s
LEFT JOIN (SELECT mmsi, string_agg(cable, ', ' ORDER BY cable) AS cables FROM lingering GROUP BY mmsi) l USING (mmsi)
LEFT JOIN (SELECT mmsi, CASE WHEN bool_or(alert = 'Alert') THEN 'Alert'
                             WHEN bool_or(alert = 'Watching') THEN 'Watching' END AS alert
           FROM alerts GROUP BY mmsi) a USING (mmsi)
ORDER BY s.mmsi
;
SET force_download = false;
SELECT * FROM fd_baltic_1
